title: Groww leads India's top brokerages in July with over 70,000 new active accounts
summary: Groww strengthened its brokerage lead in July, adding over seventy thousand active accounts.  This growth contrasts with a general industry slowdown in user additions this year.  Zerodha, the second-largest broker, continued to lose active accounts, shrinking its user base.  Angel One and Upstox Securities also experienced declines in their active client numbers.  HDFC Securities similarly shed active accounts during the month and year.

title: Godrej Consumer shares tumble on CEO exit, technicals signal more downside
summary: Godrej Consumer Products shares have experienced a notable drop following the unexpected exit of the chief executive. This abrupt change has raised significant concerns among investors about the future leadership in a volatile market environment. Aasif Malbari has been appointed as the new managing director and chief executive to steer the company.

title: Sebi sees no CAS manipulation, eyes more participation
summary: In a recent statement, Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey confirmed that the closing auction sessions showed no manipulation. He linked earlier discrepancies to cautious trading in the newly implemented system. Notably, mutual funds have significantly increased activity in these sessions. Additionally, Sebi is looking into strategies to bolster both participation and liquidity in commodity derivatives, while also striving to ease access for institutional investors within Indian markets.

title: Federal Bank, IDFC First Bank surge in credit card growth, challenging HDFC Bank
summary: Recent data reveals that Federal Bank and IDFC First Bank have collectively issued over twenty-two lakh new credit cards, almost paralleling HDFC Bank's own expansions. Together, they represent twenty-one percent of the newly released cards, suggesting a noticeable change in the competitive dynamics of the credit card sector as the dominance of the top four issuers appears to be waning.

title: Supreme Court rulings set to raise insurers' third-party liability
summary: General insurers face higher motor third-party claim reserves due to Supreme Court rulings. A recent ruling fixes homemakers' notional income, increasing claim payouts. This interpretation is expected to raise claim outgo significantly over eighteen months. Insurers also face policy standardization for occupant and pillion-rider coverage. Motor third-party insurance remains challenging with rising claim costs and slow premium growth.

title: Southern banks on a golden lending streak; gold-loan books swell 2x
summary: South Indian banks have seen their gold-loan portfolios nearly double in three years.  This significant growth is driven by rising gold prices and increased demand for credit.  Federal Bank, CSB Bank, and others experienced substantial portfolio expansions.  CSB Bank recorded the fastest growth, more than doubling its gold loan book.  Gold loans now represent a significant portion of advances for these regional lenders.

title: Banks to reveal loan rates every month in RBI's disclosure tweak
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has proposed new lending rate guidelines. Regulated entities must declare lending rates monthly and reset floating loans quarterly. Total charges for microfinance and small loans will be capped by the regulator. These new norms aim to harmonize interest rate determination methods. Final guidelines will take effect from April 1, 2027.

title: TPG, Temasek sell 13% stake in Dr Agarwals Health Care for Rs 2,008 crore
summary: Global investors TPG and Temasek sold nearly thirteen percent of Dr Agarwals Health Care. They collectively offloaded over four crore equity shares for two thousand eight crore rupees. Several mutual funds and investment firms purchased a significant stake in the eye care chain. This stake sale occurred after the company reported strong quarterly financial results. Dr Agarwals Health Care shares saw a decline following the large block deal.

title: Bank of America invests around Rs 18,268 crore for 49.9% stake in  Jio Credit
summary: Bank of America will invest up to $1.9 billion in Jio Credit. This significant foreign investment aims to acquire nearly fifty percent of the lending subsidiary. The transaction will provide substantial capital for Jio Credit's expansion plans. It will combine Jio's digital network with Bank of America's financial expertise. This partnership seeks to enhance credit access for all Indians.

title: Bank deposits hit decade-high growth as NRI dollar inflows cross $37 billion
summary: Bank deposits saw their fastest growth in nearly ten years by July. Overseas Indians deposited about $37 billion in foreign currency accounts. Bank credit growth also accelerated to its fastest pace since June 2024. This surge was driven by corporate demand and MSME lending programs. India garnered nearly $41 billion in total inflows by July 31.

title: Banks continue to garner FCNR deposits at a brisk pace
summary: Indian banks are attracting foreign currency deposits at a brisk pace.  Indian Bank and Central Bank of India have garnered substantial foreign currency deposits.  The Reserve Bank of India's special measures have brought in significant foreign exchange inflows.  These measures are largely driven by FCNR(B) deposits, exceeding previous years' collections.  Banks can swap these deposits with the RBI under a zero-cost hedging facility.
